prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: Adding an explicit hinge on the upper-tier macro COUNT ratio and macro AREA ratio (only when macros exist) keeps the raw partition macro-balanced so the official repair step flips fewer macro nodes and preserves the learned cut structure.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=-0.719 robust(mean-std)=-0.336 min_case=-0.344 seed_std=0.333 tns_mean=-0.148 all_valid=True
  C1: score=-0.110 dWNS=-11.6% dTNS=-6.3% per-seed=[+0.08 -0.56 +0.15]
  C2: score=-0.344 dWNS=-57.2% dTNS=-19.5% per-seed=[+0.06 -0.51 -0.57]
  C3: score=-0.264 dWNS=-30.6% dTNS=-14.1% per-seed=[+0.17 -0.18 -0.79]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->131, wcut 421->414, crit_cross 0.011->0.093, repair_flips 103->71, changed-vs-baseline 22.9%
  C2: cut 318->334, wcut 1007->1097, crit_cross 0.000->0.003, repair_flips 238->207, changed-vs-baseline 33.3%
  C3: cut 582->568, wcut 1955->1933, crit_cross 0.069->0.107, repair_flips 353->295, changed-vs-baseline 35.1%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis partly held: repair_flips fell on all circuits (103→71, 238→207, 353→295) and cut/wcut improved on C1/C3, but C2 worsened (cut 318→334, wcut 1007→1097) and crit_cross rose everywhere (C1 0.011→0.093). Yet scores are negative on all circuits (total −0.719), so macro-balance gains did not translate to timing; the crit_cross increase plausibly offsets fewer flips. Seed spread is high (std 0.333; C2/C3 per-seed range ~0.6–0.9), unacceptable. Next: gate the hinge weight per-circuit or add a crit_cross penalty, and re-test with more seeds.
